requirement: Describe a randomized controlled trial of a 12-week collaborative-care, home-based rehabilitation program versus attention-matched standard care after dysvascular transtibial amputation, with assessments at baseline, Week 12, and Week 24.

evidence.text: The protocol synopsis and methods define the parallel groups, intervention duration, control contacts, and three assessment times.

requirement: Randomize participants after baseline testing to experimental or control treatment and stratify allocation by sex.

evidence.text: The methods state that participants are randomized after the initial test session, stratified by sex.

requirement: Define the primary endpoint as between-group difference in Timed Up-and-Go performance at Week 12, adjusted for its baseline value.

evidence.text: TUG at Week 12 is identified as the primary outcome and endpoint.
The final model controls for baseline outcome.

requirement: Cover the protocol secondary domains: 2-minute and 5-meter walk tests, mobility and patient-specific function scales, physical activity, self-efficacy and motivation, exercise adherence, and healthcare use, including their Week 12 and Week 24 trajectories where measured.

evidence.text: The synopsis and outcomes section enumerate physical function, activity, self-management, adherence, and healthcare-use outcomes.

requirement: Plan to enroll 44 participants to retain 17 per group at Week 12, based on an expected 6.0-second TUG difference, SD 6.0, effect size 1.0, 80% power, and 20% loss to follow-up.

evidence.text: The sample-size section provides the effect, variance, power, retained sample, and attrition assumptions.

requirement: Analyze every outcome at Weeks 12 and 24 with maximum-likelihood multivariate repeated-measures modeling that uses all available observations.

evidence.text: The independent SAP replaces the protocol complete-case/exposure approach with maximum-likelihood repeated measures.

requirement: For each repeated-measures outcome, adjust for its baseline value, rehabilitation clinic type (VA versus non-VA), diabetes diagnosis, and peripheral arterial disease diagnosis.

evidence.text: The SAP lists all four adjustment terms.

requirement: State the missing-at-random assumption supporting maximum-likelihood use of all available repeated measurements, without carrying an early-termination test forward as the primary rule.

evidence.text: The protocol proposed an exposure threshold and early-termination carry-forward rule.
The final SAP instead specifies maximum likelihood under MAR.

requirement: Report estimated group means and within-group mean changes over time with 95% confidence intervals for every modeled outcome.

evidence.text: The SAP defines these effect summaries and intervals.

requirement: Treat TUG at Week 12 as the single powered confirmatory endpoint and report the multiple secondary outcomes as exploratory without multiplicity adjustment.

evidence.text: The protocol protects alpha with one primary test.
The SAP explicitly states no multiplicity adjustment for secondary endpoints.

requirement: Use two-sided alpha 0.05 for the primary TUG comparison.

evidence.text: The protocol identifies alpha 0.05 for the single primary test.

requirement: Analyze exploratory predictors of Week 24 physical activity and disability through staged regression screening across prespecified factor domains, followed by parsimonious-model comparison using adjusted R-squared and partial F tests.

evidence.text: The protocol describes the exploratory hierarchical predictor-selection process.

requirement: Summarize falls, adverse events, and serious adverse events collected continuously by randomized group and follow-up period.

evidence.text: Falls, AEs, and SAEs are collected continuously.

requirement: Document that the governing SAP changes the protocol plan from analysis restricted to at least six weeks of exposure with early-termination carry-forward to maximum-likelihood repeated measures using all available data under MAR.

evidence.text: The protocol gives the earlier exposure and carry-forward plan.
The SAP gives the later all-available-data plan.

requirement: Ask the statistical team to confirm the final analysis population, repeated-measures covariance structure, degrees-of-freedom method, handling of deaths or inability to perform TUG, and any sensitivity analysis before making these choices binding.

evidence.text: The protocol does not fully resolve these operational decisions.
The short SAP also omits covariance, degrees of freedom, and intercurrent-event rules.

notes: These are protocol-only confirmation targets rather than hidden reference-SAP facts.
